title: Measurement Conversions within a System
standard_text: 5.7A solve problems by calculating conversions within a measurement system, customary or metric
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 measurement worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.7A: customary and metric conversions, capacity and time, comparing measurements and multi-step word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: To a smaller unit: multiply. To a larger unit: divide.
key_sub: Metric units use powers of 10. Change to the same unit before comparing.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Larger unit to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller unit to larger unit: divide.
  • Metric units change by powers of 10: 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 L = 1,000 mL, 1 kg = 1,000 g.
  • Customary: 12 in. = 1 ft, 3 ft = 1 yd, 5,280 ft = 1 mi, 16 oz = 1 lb, 2 c = 1 pt, 2 pt = 1 qt, 4 qt = 1 gal.
  • Change to the same unit before you compare.

Examples

Example

3.5 km = ? m

1 km = 1,000 m

3.5 × 1,000

Answer: 3,500 m

Example

54 in. = ? ft

54 ÷ 12 = 4 R6

Answer: 4 1/2 ft

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing when changing to a smaller unitSmaller units mean more of them: multiply.
Using 10 for customary unitsCheck the table: 12, 3, 16, 4 …
Comparing 2 ft and 20 in. as 2 and 20Convert to the same unit first: 24 in. > 20 in.

faq.a: Solve problems by calculating conversions within a measurement system, customary or metric.

faq.q: Do I get a reference chart on the STAAR?
faq.a: Yes, the Grade 5 STAAR has a reference chart, but knowing common conversions saves time.
Multiply or divide by 10, 100 or 1,000 by moving the decimal point.

faq.q: How do I solve multi-step conversion problems?
faq.a: Convert first, then add, subtract, multiply or divide in the same unit.

items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 yd = 12 ft. (48 uses 12, the inches in a foot.)
1 yd = 3 ft. Yards are bigger, so divide: 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so 9 ft = 3 yd. (27 multiplies instead of dividing.)
1 ft = 12 in. Inches are smaller, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36, and 1/2 of 12 = 6. 36 + 6 = 42, so 3 1/2 ft = 42 in. (36 in forgets the half foot, and 35 in uses 10 instead of 12.)
1 mi = 5,280 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 5,280 = 10,560, so 2 mi = 10,560 ft. (2,640 divides instead of multiplying, and 3,520 is the number of yards in 2 miles.)

1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger, so divide: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6. The 6 inches left over are 6/12 of a foot = 1/2, so 30 in = 2 1/2 ft. (3 ft divides by 10. 2.6 ft is a mistake for 2 ft 6 in: 6 inches is half a foot, not 0.6 of a foot.)

1 lb = 16 oz. Pounds are bigger, so divide: 40 ÷ 16 = 2 R8. The 8 ounces left over are 8/16 of a pound = 1/2, so 40 oz = 2 1/2 lb. (4 lb divides by 10. 2.8 lb is a mistake for 2 lb 8 oz: 8 oz is half a pound, not 0.8 of a pound.)
1 ft = 12 in, so 4 ft = 4 × 12 = 48 in. Add the leftover inches: 48 + 9 = 57 in. (49 in uses 10 instead of 12, and 48 in forgets the 9 inches.)
1 lb = 16 oz. Pounds are bigger, so divide: 8 ÷ 16. 8 oz is 8/16 of a pound = 1/2, so 8 oz = 1/2 lb. (2 lb divides 16 by 8, the wrong way round.)
1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger, so divide: 18 ÷ 12 = 1 R6. The 6 inches left over are 6/12 of a foot = 1/2, so 18 in = 1 1/2 ft. (6 ft divides by 3, the feet in a yard.)
1 lb = 16 oz. Ounces are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 16 = 32, and 3/4 of 16 = 12. 32 + 12 = 44, so 2 3/4 lb = 44 oz. (32 oz forgets the 3/4 pound, and 27.5 oz uses 10 instead of 16.)
1 lb = 16 oz, so 6 lb = 6 × 16 = 96 oz. Add the leftover ounces: 96 + 5 = 101 oz. (65 oz writes the digits side by side, and 77 oz uses 12 instead of 16.)
1 ton = 2,000 lb. Tons are bigger, so divide: 4,000 ÷ 2,000 = 2, so 4,000 lb = 2 tons. (4 tons divides by 1,000, and 250 tons divides by 16, the ounces in a pound.)

1 ton = 2,000 lb. Pounds are smaller, so multiply: 1 × 2,000 = 2,000, and 1/2 of 2,000 = 1,000. 2,000 + 1,000 = 3,000, so 1 1/2 tons = 3,000 lb. (1,500 lb uses 1,000 instead of 2,000, and 24 lb uses 16, the ounces in a pound.)
1 yd = 3 ft, so 1 yd 2 ft = 3 + 2 = 5 ft. 1 ft = 12 in, so 5 ft = 5 × 12 = 60 in. (36 in forgets the 2 feet, and 38 in adds 2 inches instead of 2 feet.)
1 ft = 12 in. 42 ÷ 12 = 3 R6: 3 whole feet and 6 inches left over, so 42 in = 3 ft 6 in. Check: 36 + 6 = 42. (4 ft 2 in divides by 10.)
1 mi = 5,280 ft. Miles are bigger, so divide: 2,640 ÷ 5,280. 2,640 is half of 5,280, so 2,640 ft = 1/2 mi. (2 mi divides 5,280 by 2,640, the wrong way round. 2.64 mi divides by 1,000.)
1 mi = 5,280 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 1/4 of 5,280 = 5,280 ÷ 4 = 1,320, so 1/4 mi = 1,320 ft. (21,120 multiplies by 4 instead of finding one fourth, and 2,640 ft is half a mile.)
1 yd = 3 ft. Feet are smaller, so multiply: 3 × 3 = 9, and 1/3 of 3 = 1. 9 + 1 = 10, so 3 1/3 yd = 10 ft. (9 1/3 ft forgets to multiply the 1/3 by 3.)
1 lb = 16 oz. 52 ÷ 16 = 3 R4: 3 whole pounds and 4 ounces left over, so 52 oz = 3 lb 4 oz. Check: 48 + 4 = 52. (5 lb 2 oz divides by 10, and 4 lb 4 oz uses 12 instead of 16.)

1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger, so divide: 75 ÷ 12 = 6 R3. The 3 inches left over are 3/12 of a foot = 1/4, so 75 in = 6 1/4 ft. (7.5 ft divides by 10. 6.3 ft and 6 1/3 ft both treat the 3 leftover inches as 3 tenths or 1 third of a foot.)
1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so there will be more meters: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 3.5 × 1,000 = 3,500, so 3.5 km = 3,500 m.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be more centimeters: multiply by 100. The point moves 2 places right: 4.2 × 100 = 420, so 4.2 m = 420 cm.
1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so there will be more grams: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 0.6 × 1,000 = 600, so 0.6 kg = 600 g.
1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so there will be more milliliters: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 1.25 × 1,000 = 1,250, so 1.25 L = 1,250 mL.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 100. The point moves 2 places left: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 250 cm = 2.5 m.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 100. The point moves 2 places left: 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05, so 5 cm = 0.05 m.
1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75, so 750 g = 0.75 kg.
1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 3,200 ÷ 1,000 = 3.2, so 3,200 m = 3.2 km.

items.q: To change 2,400 g to kilograms, what do you do?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. A kilogram is bigger than a gram, so there will be fewer kilograms: divide by 1,000. 2,400 ÷ 1,000 = 2.4, so 2,400 g = 2.4 kg.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 100. 275 ÷ 100 = 2.75 (the point moves 2 places left).
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimeters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be more millimeters: multiply by 10. The point moves 1 place right: 0.8 × 10 = 8, so 0.8 cm = 8 mm.
1 m = 1,000 mm. Meters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be more millimeters: multiply by 1,000. The point moves 3 places right: 2.75 × 1,000 = 2,750, so 2.75 m = 2,750 mm.
1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so there will be more centimeters: multiply by 100. The point moves 2 places right: 0.4 × 100 = 40, so 0.4 m = 40 cm.

items.q: You change 6.8 m to centimeters. How does the decimal point move?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply by 100. 100 has 2 zeros, and multiplying makes the number bigger, so the point moves 2 places right: 6.8 m = 680 cm.
1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 600 ÷ 1,000 = 0.6, so 600 mL = 0.6 L.
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimeters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 10. The point moves 1 place left: 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5, so 45 mm = 4.5 cm.
1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 80 ÷ 1,000 = 0.08, so 80 g = 0.08 kg.
1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 1,500 ÷ 1,000 = 1.5, so 1,500 mL = 1.5 L.
1 m = 1,000 mm. Meters are bigger than millimeters, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 1,000. The point moves 3 places left: 350 ÷ 1,000 = 0.35, so 350 mm = 0.35 m.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 1,000. 1,750 ÷ 1,000 = 1.75 (the point moves 3 places left).
1 qt = 2 pt. Pints are smaller, so multiply: 3 × 2 = 6, so 3 qt = 6 pt. (12 pt uses 4, the quarts in a gallon, and 1 1/2 pt divides instead of multiplying.)
1 pt = 2 cups. Pints are bigger, so divide: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so 6 cups = 3 pt. (12 pt multiplies instead of dividing, and 1 1/2 pt divides by 4, the cups in a quart.)
1 gal = 4 qt. Quarts are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 4 = 8, so 2 gal = 8 qt. (4 qt multiplies by 2 instead of 4, and 16 is the number of pints in 2 gallons.)
1 gal = 4 qt. Gallons are bigger, so divide: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 12 qt = 3 gal. (48 gal multiplies instead of dividing, and 6 gal divides by 2, the pints in a quart.)
1 gal = 4 qt and 1 qt = 4 cups, so 1 gal = 16 cups. Half of 16 is 8 cups. (2 cups is the number of quarts in 1/2 gallon, and 32 cups doubles instead of halving.)
1 gal = 4 qt, so 3 gal = 3 × 4 = 12 qt. Add the leftover quarts: 12 + 2 = 14 qt. (32 qt writes the digits side by side, and 8 qt uses 2 instead of 4.)
1 qt = 2 pt. Quarts are bigger, so divide: 5 ÷ 2 = 2 R1. The 1 pint left over is 1/2 of a quart, so 5 pt = 2 1/2 qt. (1 1/4 qt divides by 4, and 2 1/4 qt treats the leftover pint as 1/4 quart.)

1 gal = 4 qt. Gallons are bigger, so divide: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 R2. The 2 quarts left over are 2/4 of a gallon = 1/2, so 10 qt = 2 1/2 gal. (2.2 gal is a mistake for 2 gal 2 qt: 2 quarts is half a gallon, not 0.2 of a gallon.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 4. 10 ÷ 4 = 2 R2, and 2 quarts is 2/4 = 1/2 gallon, so the answer is 2 1/2. (5 divides by 2, and 2.2 is a mistake for 2 gal 2 qt.)
1 qt = 4 cups. Quarts are bigger, so divide: 3 ÷ 4. 3 cups is 3/4 of a quart, so 3 cups = 3/4 qt. (12 qt multiplies instead of dividing, and 1 1/2 qt divides by 2, the cups in a pint.)

1 hr = 60 min. Hours are bigger, so divide: 90 ÷ 60 = 1 R30. The 30 minutes left over are 30/60 of an hour = 1/2, so 90 min = 1 1/2 hr. (9 hr divides by 10 and 0.9 hr divides by 100. 1.3 hr is a mistake for 1 hr 30 min.)

items.q: Which is the same as 1.5 hours?
items.e: 1.5 hours is 1 hour and half an hour. Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes, so 1.5 hr = 1 hr 30 min = 90 min. The .5 means one half, not 50 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.
1 hr = 60 min. Hours are bigger, so divide: 45 ÷ 60. 45 min is 45/60 of an hour = 3/4, so 45 min = 3/4 hr. (0.45 hr divides by 100, and 2,700 hr multiplies instead of dividing.)
0.25 = 1/4. 1 hr = 60 min, and 1/4 of 60 = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 min. (25 min reads the decimal as minutes, and 240 min divides 60 by 0.25.)

1 min = 60 sec. Minutes are bigger, so divide: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 R30. The 30 seconds left over are 30/60 of a minute = 1/2, so 150 sec = 2 1/2 min. (1.5 min divides by 100. 2.3 min is a mistake for 2 min 30 sec.)
1 hr = 60 min. Minutes are smaller, so multiply: 2 × 60 = 120, and 1/4 of 60 = 15. 120 + 15 = 135, so 2 1/4 hr = 135 min. (225 min uses 100 instead of 60, and 120 min forgets the 1/4 hour.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min, so every number on the right is the left number ÷ 60. 105 ÷ 60 = 1 R45, and 45 minutes is 45/60 = 3/4 of an hour, so the answer is 1 3/4. (1.05 divides by 100, 10 1/2 divides by 10, and 6,300 multiplies instead of dividing.)
1 day = 24 hr. Days are bigger, so divide: 36 ÷ 24 = 1 R12. The 12 hours left over are 12/24 of a day = 1/2, so 36 hr = 1 1/2 days. (3 days divides by 12. 1.2 days is a mistake for 1 day 12 hours.)
1 hr = 60 min. 200 ÷ 60 = 3 R20: 3 whole hours and 20 minutes left over, so 200 min = 3 hr 20 min. Check: 180 + 20 = 200. (2 hr uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: Which is the same as 3 1/4 hours?
items.e: 1/4 of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes, so 3 1/4 hr = 3 hr 15 min = 195 min. (3 hr 25 min reads 1/4 as 0.25, and 3 hr 4 min uses the 4 from the fraction.)
Change everything to centimeters: 1.2 m = 120 cm, 1,150 mm = 115 cm and 1 m 25 cm = 125 cm. In order: 125 cm, 120 cm, 115 cm, 98 cm. So the answer is 1 m 25 cm.
Change everything to grams: 0.8 kg = 800 g and 0.09 kg = 90 g (not 900 g). In order: 820 g, 800 g, 750 g, 90 g. So the answer is 820 g.
Change everything to milliliters: 0.5 L = 500 mL and 0.05 L = 50 mL. In order: 50 mL, 120 mL, 450 mL, 500 mL. So the answer is 0.05 L.
Change everything to grams: 1.05 kg = 1,050 g and 1.5 kg = 1,500 g. In order: 1,010 g, 1,050 g, 1,100 g, 1,500 g. So the answer is 1,010 g.
2 ft = 24 in, and 1/2 ft = 6 in, so 2 1/2 ft = 30 in. Half a foot is 6 inches, not 5, and 30 in is not 3 ft because 1 ft = 12 in, not 10.

items.q: Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: Change them to the same unit: 0.5 m = 500 mm and 6 cm = 60 mm, and 8 < 60 < 500. The biggest number is not always the longest length. So the order is 8 mm, 6 cm, 0.5 m.
Change everything to inches: 2 1/2 ft = 24 + 6 = 30 in, 1 yd = 36 in and 2 ft 8 in = 24 + 8 = 32 in. In order: 36 in, 32 in, 30 in, 28 in. So the answer is 1 yd.
Change everything to ounces: 2 1/4 lb = 32 + 4 = 36 oz and 2 lb 5 oz = 32 + 5 = 37 oz. In order: 37 oz, 36 oz, 35 oz, 34 oz. So the answer is 2 lb 5 oz.
2.5 hr = 2 hours and half an hour = 120 + 30 = 150 min. The .5 is one half of 60 minutes, which is 30 minutes, not 50.
Change everything to cups: 3 qt = 12 cups, 5 pt = 10 cups and 1 gal = 16 cups. In order: 16 cups, 14 cups, 12 cups, 10 cups. So the answer is 1 gal.

items.q: Which is the longest amount of time?
items.e: Change everything to minutes: 1 1/2 hr = 90 min, 1 hr 35 min = 95 min and 1 3/4 hr = 60 + 45 = 105 min. In order: 105 min, 100 min, 95 min, 90 min. So the answer is 1 3/4 hr.
1 qt = 2 pt, so 3 pt is more than 1 qt: 3 pt > 1 qt. 3 pt is only 3/8 gal, and 2 qt = 8 cups, which is more than 6 cups.

items.q: Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: Change them to the same unit: 1 1/4 ft = 12 + 3 = 15 in and 1 ft 1 in = 12 + 1 = 13 in, and 13 < 15 < 16. So the order is 1 ft 1 in, 1 1/4 ft, 16 in.
1 lb = 16 oz. 1/4 of 16 is 4, so 3/4 of 16 is 3 × 4 = 12. 3/4 lb = 12 oz, which is less than 1 lb.

items.q: Which is NOT equal to 2 qt?
items.e: 1 qt = 2 pt = 4 cups, so 2 qt = 4 pt = 8 cups. 1 gal = 4 qt, so 1/2 gal = 2 qt too. 6 cups is only 1 1/2 qt.

items.q: Which list goes from greatest to least?
items.e: Change them to the same unit: 2 hr = 120 min and 1 3/4 hr = 60 + 45 = 105 min, and 120 > 110 > 105. So the order is 2 hr, 110 min, 1 3/4 hr.
Change everything to feet: 1/2 mi = 5,280 ÷ 2 = 2,640 ft and 900 yd = 900 × 3 = 2,700 ft. In order: 2,500 ft, 2,640 ft, 2,700 ft, 3,000 ft. So the answer is 2,500 ft.

items.q: Which is NOT equal to 1.5 m?
items.e: 1.5 m = 150 cm = 1,500 mm = 1 m 50 cm. 1 m 5 cm is only 105 cm: the .5 means 50 cm, not 5 cm.

items.q: Harper has a ribbon 2 m long. She cuts it into pieces that are 25 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: Use the same unit: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 ÷ 25 = 8 pieces. (80 uses 1 m = 1,000 cm, 50 multiplies 2 × 25, and 4 uses only 1 m.)

items.q: A store sells rice in 750 g bags. What is the total mass of 6 bags in kilograms?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 750 = 4,500 g. Step 2: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so divide: 4,500 ÷ 1,000 = 4.5 kg. (4,500 kg forgets to convert.)

items.q: A track is 400 m around. Zoe runs 12 laps. How many kilometers does she run?
A snail moves 5 cm each minute. How many meters does it move in 1 hour?
items.e: Step 1: 1 hr = 60 min, so 60 × 5 = 300 cm. Step 2: 1 m = 100 cm, so 300 ÷ 100 = 3 m. (300 m forgets to convert.)

items.q: A cooler holds 3 gal of water. How many 1-pint bottles can be filled from it?
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt and 1 qt = 2 pt, so 1 gal = 8 pt. 3 × 8 = 24 bottles. (12 counts quarts, and 48 counts cups.)

items.q: A recipe uses 3/4 cup of milk. Jayden makes 4 batches. How many pints of milk does he need?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × 3/4 = 12/4 = 3 cups. Step 2: 2 cups = 1 pt, so 3 ÷ 2 = 1 1/2 pt. (3 pt forgets to convert, and 6 pt multiplies by 2 instead of dividing.)

items.q: Lemonade is made with 10 qt of water and 6 pt of juice. How many gallons of lemonade is that?
items.e: Step 1: 6 pt = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 qt, so the total is 10 + 3 = 13 qt. Step 2: 4 qt = 1 gal, so 13 ÷ 4 = 3 R1 = 3 1/4 gal. (4 gal adds 10 + 6 without changing pints to quarts, and 13 gal forgets to change quarts to gallons.)

items.q: Valeria has a 5 m rope. She cuts off 3 pieces that are each 85 cm long. How many meters of rope are left?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 85 = 255 cm = 2.55 m cut off. Step 2: 5 − 2.55 = 2.45 m. (2.55 m is the part cut off, 4.15 m subtracts only one piece, and 4.745 m treats 255 cm as 0.255 m.)

items.q: Mia has a 1.5 L bottle of water. She drinks 350 mL in the morning and 0.4 L in the afternoon. How many milliliters are left?
A movie is 2 1/4 hours long. Ethan has watched 85 minutes. How many minutes are left?
items.e: Step 1: 2 1/4 hr = 120 + 15 = 135 min. Step 2: 135 − 85 = 50 min. (60 min reads 2 1/4 hr as 2 hr 25 min, and 35 min forgets the 1/4 hour.)

items.q: A puppy weighed 3 lb when it was born. Now it weighs 10 lb 8 oz. How many ounces has it gained?
items.e: Step 1: 10 lb 8 oz − 3 lb = 7 lb 8 oz. Step 2: 7 × 16 = 112, and 112 + 8 = 120 oz. (78 oz uses 10 ounces in a pound, and 168 oz is the puppy's weight now.)

items.q: A shelf is 3 ft long. Each book on it is 1 1/2 in thick. How many books fit on the shelf?
items.e: Step 1: 3 ft = 3 × 12 = 36 in. Step 2: 36 ÷ 1 1/2 = 24 books (2 books fill 3 inches, and 36 ÷ 3 × 2 = 24). (2 books forgets to change feet to inches, and 20 uses 10 inches in a foot.)

items.q: A baker has 3 bags of flour. Each bag holds 2.5 kg. A loaf of bread uses 500 g. How many loaves can the baker make?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 kg = 7,500 g. Step 2: 7,500 ÷ 500 = 15 loaves. (5 loaves uses only 1 bag, and 150 loaves changes 7.5 kg to 75,000 g instead of 7,500 g, and 1 1/2 loaves changes 2.5 kg to 250 g.)

items.q: Punch is made with 1 qt of orange juice, 3 pt of apple juice and 6 cups of ginger ale. How many cups of punch is that?
items.e: Change to cups: 1 qt = 4 cups and 3 pt = 3 × 2 = 6 cups. 4 + 6 + 6 = 16 cups, which is exactly 1 gal. (10 adds the numbers without converting.)

items.q: Nevaeh practices soccer for 1 hr 45 min, 4 days a week. How long does she practice each week?
items.e: Step 1: 1 hr 45 min = 105 min, and 4 × 105 = 420 min. Step 2: 420 ÷ 60 = 7 hr. (5.8 hr multiplies 1.45 × 4, as if an hour had 100 minutes, and 4 hr 45 min multiplies only the hours.)

items.q: A truck can carry 2 tons. Each crate weighs 250 lb. How many crates can the truck carry?
items.e: Step 1: 1 ton = 2,000 lb, so 2 tons = 4,000 lb. Step 2: 4,000 ÷ 250 = 16 crates. (8 crates uses only 1 ton, 160 crates divides by 25 instead of 250, and 500 crates multiplies 2 × 250.)

items.q: Gabriel walks 1/4 mi to school and 1/4 mi back home, 5 days a week. How many feet does he walk in a week?
items.e: Step 1: 1/4 mi = 5,280 ÷ 4 = 1,320 ft. Step 2: each day 2 × 1,320 = 2,640 ft. Step 3: 5 × 2,640 = 13,200 ft. (6,600 ft counts only the walk to school.)

items.q: A backpack can hold 5 kg. Carlos puts in 3 books of 650 g each and a laptop of 1.8 kg. How many more kilograms can the backpack hold?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 650 = 1,950 g = 1.95 kg. Step 2: 1.95 + 1.8 = 3.75 kg in the bag. Step 3: 5 − 3.75 = 1.25 kg. (3.75 kg is what is already in the bag, and 2.55 kg counts only one book.)

items.q: Josiah practices piano for 3/4 hr on Monday, 50 min on Tuesday and 1 1/4 hr on Wednesday. How many minutes is that in all?
items.e: Change to minutes: 3/4 hr = 45 min and 1 1/4 hr = 60 + 15 = 75 min. 45 + 50 + 75 = 170 min (2 hr 50 min). (250 min uses 100 minutes in an hour, and 110 min forgets the 1 in 1 1/4 hr.)

items.q: Elijah has 4 yd of ribbon. Each bow uses 2 ft 6 in. How many whole bows can he make?
items.e: Use inches: 4 yd = 4 × 36 = 144 in and 2 ft 6 in = 30 in. 144 ÷ 30 = 4 R24, so 4 bows, with 24 in left over. (5 rounds up, but there is not enough ribbon for a 5th bow. 6 ignores the 6 inches: 12 ft ÷ 2 ft.)
